suppress.notes: TIER 1. org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql is a Java test support module: it starts a PostgreSQL container for integration tests and contains no database engine code whatsoever. Dependency-Check matched its Maven version 2.0.3 against cpe:/a:postgresql:postgresql, that is against PostgreSQL SERVER version 2.0.3, and attached the server advisory history for that version to it. Twenty six records at CVSS 7 or above arrived this way, the oldest from 2015. The mismatch is a property of the artifact, not of any one advisory, so the CPE is removed rather than the CVEs. The actual PostgreSQL server this project runs is the pinned postgres:16.14-alpine image in docker-compose.yml, which is not a Maven dependency and is not in scope for this scanner. The JDBC driver org.postgresql:postgresql is a separate dependency and is scanned on its own identity; see its entry below. Scope: test.

TIER 1. io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus is a Java library that EXPOSES metrics in the Prometheus exposition format. It is not the Prometheus server, which is a separate product written in Go and, in this project, the pinned prom/prometheus:v3.5.5 container in docker-compose.yml. Dependency-Check matched the Micrometer version 1.15.9 against cpe:/a:prometheus:prometheus. The single record this produced, CVE-2026-42154, is a heap exhaustion in the Prometheus server's remote read endpoint /api/v1/read. No such endpoint, and no snappy request decoder, exists in this library; the only surface it provides is the scrape endpoint the server calls.

TIER 1. org.eclipse.angus:angus-activation is the Jakarta ACTIVATION implementation. Dependency-Check matched it to cpe:/a:eclipse:angus_mail, the Jakarta MAIL implementation, and did so at LOW confidence, which the report itself records. The one record that followed, CVE-2025-7962, is an SMTP header injection in Jakarta Mail. Two independent facts make it inapplicable: this is a different artifact, and org.eclipse.angus:angus-mail is not on the dependency graph at all. CardDemo sends no mail; there is no SMTP client anywhere in the target architecture. angus-activation is present only because Jakarta Activation is a transitive requirement of the validation and XML binding stack.

TIER 1. io.opentelemetry.semconv:opentelemetry-semconv is a Java artifact containing nothing but generated semantic convention attribute-key constants. Dependency-Check matched it to cpe:/a:opentelemetry:opentelemetry and attached two records, CVE-2026-24051 and CVE-2026-39883, both at 7.0. Both advisories state their subject in their own first sentence: "OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry". Both are PATH hijacking in resource detection code, naming the Go source file sdk/resource/host_id.go and the ioreg and kenv system commands on Darwin, BSD and Solaris. This artifact is Java, executes no external command, and contains no resource detector. The Java tracing path in this project is micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel with opentelemetry-exporter-otlp, both of which are scanned on their own identities.

TIER 1. Every spring-boot-starter-* artifact is a dependency AGGREGATOR rather than a code artifact. A jar listing at 3.5.11 of all thirteen starters resolved by this build - starter, -web, -actuator, -batch, -data-jpa, -jdbc, -json, -logging, -oauth2-resource-server, -security, -test, -tomcat and -validation - reports ZERO .class entries in every one of them, so no starter can contain a vulnerable class. spring-boot-starter-web is the artifact the scanner flagged first. Its jar was inspected and contains ZERO .class files; its entire content is a POM that pulls in spring-web, spring-webmvc, spring-boot-autoconfigure and the embedded container. Dependency-Check nevertheless assigned it cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot version 3.5.11 and attached ALL EIGHT Spring Boot product advisories for that version to it, and additionally assigned the generic cpe:/a:web_project:web. The count is a reading of the report, not an estimate: the starter's entry lists eight suppressed records. No advisory can be exploited through an artifact that contains no code. The jars that DO carry the Spring Boot code, spring-boot, spring-boot-actuator and spring-boot-autoconfigure, are separate dependencies and were evaluated independently in the same scan; nothing is hidden by removing these two CPEs from the aggregator. For the record, SEVEN OF THE EIGHT are also inapplicable on their own terms - the eighth, CVE-2026-40977, is not, and is dealt with at the end of this note: CVE-2026-40974 is Cassandra auto-configuration and no Cassandra driver is present; CVE-2026-40971 is RabbitMQ auto-configuration and no AMQP client is present; CVE-2026-22733 requires the CloudFoundry Actuator extension, which requires running on CloudFoundry; CVE-2026-40972 is the spring-boot-devtools remote secret and devtools is not a dependency; CVE-2026-40975 warns that ${random.value} is unfit for secrets, and the one secret this application has, the JWT signing key, is required from the JWT_SIGNING_KEY environment variable with no generated default; CVE-2026-40973 requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and this application is stateless by architectural mandate, holding no server side session at all; CVE-2026-22731 is discussed in its own Tier 4 entry below. THE EIGHTH, CVE-2026-40977, IS NOT DISMISSED. A PID file write that follows symlinks at a predictable default path is a real defect of the Spring Boot code at this version, and nothing here claims otherwise. It is also the proof that removing these two CPEs from the aggregator hides nothing: in the same scan that suppresses it on this CODELESS starter, CVE-2026-40977 is reported ACTIVE against spring-boot-3.5.11.jar, the jar that does carry the code, and it stays active - unsuppressed anywhere in this file - because at CVSS 6.7 it falls under the failBuildOnCVSS 7 gate on its own score. It is disclosed as residual risk in pom.xml instead.

TIER 1. Same zero-class aggregator argument as the entry immediately above, applied to the other identifier the scanner attached to the starters, for the cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot identifier on both web starters. Both jars were inspected and contain ZERO .class files. The Spring Boot code jars are scanned separately on their own identities.

TIER 1. cpe:/a:web_project:web is a generic identifier for an unrelated product named "web" and was matched purely because these artifact names end in "-web" and their versions happened to align. The correct Spring identifiers on the same artifacts are retained, so both remain fully evaluated against the Spring Framework and Spring Security advisory sets.

TIER 1. cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-modules-java8 was matched against jackson-databind at LOW confidence, which the report records. The java8 modules are separate artifacts (jackson-datatype-jsr310, jackson-module-parameter-names) and are scanned under their own coordinates. The correct identifiers cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-databind and cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-core are retained.

TIER 1. cpe:/a:validator:validator was matched against org.hibernate.validator:hibernate-validator on the strength of the artefactId ending in "validator". The product behind that identifier is the Nu Html Checker, distributed as validator.nu / vnu - an HTML document validation SERVICE that fetches user supplied URLs. Hibernate Validator is the Jakarta Bean Validation reference implementation and fetches nothing. They share four letters of a name and no code. WHAT FLOWS FROM THE WRONG IDENTIFIER TODAY: CVE-2025-15104, a server side request forgery restriction bypass in the Nu Html Checker, where hostname based blocking of loopback destinations can be defeated by DNS rebinding. Hibernate Validator resolves no URLs and performs no outbound HTTP, so the described weakness has no counterpart in it. WHY THE CPE IS SUPPRESSED RATHER THAN THE CVE: the advisory records its affected version as an upstream source COMMIT, not a release number, so the range can never be cleared by a version comparison. Every hibernate-validator version matches forever - which was confirmed directly by resolving 9.1.3.Final and re-running this scan, which reported the identical CVE against hibernate-validator-9.1.3.Final.jar under the same CPE. Removing the identifier therefore also carries any FUTURE validator.nu advisory that would be misattributed the same way, which suppressing one CVE would not. The same false positive is tracked upstream against other unrelated Maven artefacts whose coordinate ends in "validator". NOT SUPPRESSED: no other identifier for this artefact is touched, so a real Hibernate Validator advisory would still fail the build.

TIER 2. All four advisories name classes that live in Log4j CORE or in the Log4j 1 bridge, never in log4j-api: CVE-2026-34478 org.apache.logging.log4j.core.layout.Rfc5424Layout CVE-2026-34479 Log4j1XmlLayout, from the log4j-1.2-api bridge CVE-2026-34480 org.apache.logging.log4j.core.layout.XmlLayout CVE-2026-34481 JsonTemplateLayout, from log4j-layout-template-json Two independent verifications: a grep of the resolved dependency list for log4j-core, log4j-layout-template-json and log4j-1.2-api returns zero matches, and a listing of log4j-api-2.24.3.jar contains zero classes whose name matches Rfc5424Layout, XmlLayout, JsonTemplateLayout or Log4j1XmlLayout. log4j-api is present only as the facade required by log4j-to-slf4j, which routes any Log4j API call into SLF4J and from there into Logback. No Log4j layout, appender or configuration is ever instantiated, because no Log4j implementation exists to instantiate one.

TIER 2. CVE-2026-53914, CVSS 9.8, is code execution "via unsafe deserialization in the BUILD CACHE METADATA" of the JetBrains Kotlin toolchain. The vulnerable component is the Kotlin compiler's incremental build cache, not the runtime standard library. This project contains no Kotlin source file, runs no Kotlin compiler, and produces no Kotlin build cache: it is a Maven Java 25 build whose only compiler plugin is maven-compiler-plugin. kotlin-stdlib is present solely as a runtime scoped transitive of the AWS SDK dependency chain. The attacker controlled artifact the advisory requires cannot exist here because the component that would read it is never invoked. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the Kotlin standard library ships as four sibling artifacts on this graph - kotlin-stdlib, kotlin-stdlib-common, kotlin-stdlib-jdk7 and kotlin-stdlib-jdk8 - and Dependency-Check attaches the same JetBrains Kotlin identifier to every one of them. The argument above is a property of the BUILD (no Kotlin source, no Kotlin compilation, no Kotlin build cache), so it holds identically for all four; the pattern therefore enumerates the four module suffixes explicitly rather than wildcarding the JetBrains group.

TIER 2. CVE-2026-56816, CVSS 7.5, is unbounded buffering of HTTP/3 reserved frame payloads in io.netty.handler.codec.http3.Http3FrameCodec, reachable only by opening QUIC streams against an HTTP/3 endpoint. The class lives in netty-codec-http3, which is NOT on this dependency graph. The Netty modules that resolve here are exactly buffer, codec, codec-http, codec-http2, common, handler, resolver, transport, transport-classes-epoll and transport-native-unix-common; there is no codec-http3, no QUIC transport and no HTTP/3 listener anywhere in the target, whose only network server is the embedded Tomcat servlet container speaking HTTP/1.1. WHY THIS IS A SUPPRESSION AND NOT AN UPGRADE: Netty is not named by the requirements and was therefore already pinned FORWARD at the root of this build - io.netty:netty-bom 4.1.136.Final in dependencyManagement - which closed thirty-three earlier records by removing the vulnerable code rather than by argument. This one advisory has no fix on the 4.1 line: the vendor fixed it in 4.2.16.Final only, and adopting the 4.2 line would change the transport implementation underneath the AWS SDK asynchronous client, which is a substrate change the requirements do not authorise. Because the affected module is absent from the graph, the 4.1 line carries no exposure. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the record was reported against netty-transport, but Dependency-Check attaches the same Netty product identifier to every io.netty module, so the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE.

TIER 3. Both advisories are defects in jackson-databind's polymorphic deserialization guard and both require POLYMORPHIC TYPING TO BE ENABLED: CVE-2026-54512 PolymorphicTypeValidator is bypassed when polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier is supplied. CVE-2026-54513 BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder. allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists an array type without validating its component type. Polymorphic typing is not enabled anywhere in this project, and that is enforced rather than merely true today. A search of all main and test sources for JsonTypeInfo, JsonSubTypes, activateDefaultTyping, enableDefaultTyping, PolymorphicTypeValidator and DefaultTyping returns exactly two hits, both in src/test/java/com/cardemo/unit/model/SignOnResponseTest.java, and both belong to a test named "carries no polymorphic type identifier, which would be a deserialisation gadget surface" that ASSERTS THE ABSENCE of @JsonTypeInfo and asserts that no type identifier appears on the wire under any of its usual spellings. That test fails if anyone enables the feature, at which point this suppression must be removed. No ObjectMapper in this project calls activateDefaultTyping, and every DTO is a concrete final shape derived from a BMS symbolic map.

TIER 3. Six Spring Boot 3.5.11 advisories, every one of which names an auto-configuration or a feature that is not present in this application. The affected code is in the spring-boot code jar, so no class absence argument is claimed; each argument below is a verified absence of the feature the advisory requires. CVE-2026-40974 9.8 Cassandra SSL auto-configuration omits hostname verification. There is no Cassandra dependency on the graph: the datastore is PostgreSQL 16 reached through the pgjdbc driver, and a search of the resolved dependency tree for "cassandra" returns zero matches. The auto-configuration cannot activate. CVE-2026-40971 9.1 RabbitMQ auto-configuration omits hostname verification when using an SSL bundle. There is no RabbitMQ or Spring AMQP dependency on the graph - zero matches for "rabbit" - and the target's only queue is an SQS FIFO queue reached through Spring Cloud AWS, replacing the legacy transient data queue. CVE-2026-22733 8.1 authentication bypass when an authenticated endpoint is declared under the path used by the CloudFoundry Actuator endpoints. The CloudFoundry Actuator endpoints are enabled only under a CloudFoundry deployment and its management.cloudfoundry configuration; a search of the whole repository for "cloudfoundry" returns zero matches, and deployment is Docker Compose with Kubernetes and service mesh explicitly out of scope. CVE-2026-40972 7.0 timing attack against the spring-boot-devtools remote secret, leading to class upload and remote code execution. spring-boot-devtools is not a dependency of this build - zero matches on the graph and zero in the build file - so there is no remote secret, no remote restart endpoint and no upload path. CVE-2026-40973 7.0 a local attacker taking control of the ApplicationTemp directory can read session information when server.servlet.session.persistent is true. That property is set nowhere in this repository and its framework default is false. The requirements mandate stateless request handling with no server side session state at all: the legacy pseudo-conversational COMMAREA collapses into JWT claims and request parameters, so there is no session to persist. CVE-2026-40975 7.5 values produced by ${random.value} are unfit for use as secrets. No property placeholder of that form exists anywhere in this repository. The one secret in the system, the JWT signing key, is resolved from an environment variable in every profile with fail fast on absence and no committed default, which is the mechanism the requirements mandate. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: the six do NOT share one fixed release. Five of them - CVE-2026-40971, CVE-2026-40972, CVE-2026-40973, CVE-2026-40974 and CVE-2026-40975 - are fixed in Spring Boot 3.5.14, which is the release whose announcement names them. CVE-2026-22733 is fixed earlier, in Spring Boot 3.5.12, alongside its sibling CVE-2026-22731. So 3.5.14 is the EARLIEST SINGLE RELEASE that carries all six fixes, which is not the same claim as all six having been fixed in it, and the distinction is recorded here because an upgrade decision made from the weaker claim would misjudge how far the parent must move to clear any given one of them. This project pins spring-boot-starter-parent at 3.5.11 because the requirements pin it explicitly and forbid advancing it unilaterally, directing instead that the divergence be recorded. This entry is that record. If any of the six features above is ever adopted - Cassandra, RabbitMQ, a CloudFoundry deployment, devtools, persistent sessions or ${random.value} - the corresponding argument collapses and this suppression must be narrowed or removed before that change ships. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the records were reported against the spring-boot code jar, but Dependency-Check attaches the same cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot product identifier to spring-boot-autoconfigure, spring-boot-actuator and the starter aggregators as well. The arguments are properties of the APPLICATION and of the RESOLVED BOOT VERSION 3.5.11, identical across the group, so the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with six named CVEs.

TIER 3. Both records come from httpcore5 5.3.6 SHADED INSIDE com.github.docker-java:docker-java-transport-zerodep, a TEST SCOPE artifact: CVE-2026-54399 unbounded memory in the HTTP/1.1 message parser when a peer sends excessive headers. CVE-2026-54428 unbounded memory in the HTTP/2 HPACK decoder when a peer sends oversized compressed header blocks. Both require a hostile PEER able to send crafted HTTP messages. The only peer this transport ever speaks to is the local Docker daemon, reached over a unix domain socket by Testcontainers while integration tests run. It is never exposed to a network, never reachable by an untrusted party, and never present in the shipped artifact: the Spring Boot fat JAR contains compile and runtime scope only, so this code does not exist in production. The version cannot be remediated here even in principle: httpcore5 is relocated inside the zerodep jar and is therefore not reachable by Maven dependency management, and the parent artifact arrives through Testcontainers 2.0.3, which the requirements pin exactly. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: fixed in Apache HttpComponents Core later than 5.4.2. Remediation is a future Testcontainers release that shades a newer core.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. CVE-2026-22731, CVSS 8.1: a Spring Boot Actuator authentication bypass when an authenticated application endpoint is declared under a path already configured as a Health Group additional path. This application does expose Actuator with liveness and readiness health groups, so the feature family is present and no inapplicability is claimed. It is recorded here rather than under the aggregator entry above precisely because it is the one of the eight Spring Boot advisories that can neither be dismissed on its own terms nor left to the gate to absorb. Of the other seven, six are inapplicable to this application and the last, CVE-2026-40977, is applicable but scores CVSS 6.7, under the threshold, so it needs no entry and has none. WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED HERE. Fixed in Spring Boot 3.5.12. The advisory's own prose reads "from 3.5 before 3.5.11" while its machine readable affected range is 3.5.0 to before 3.5.12; Dependency-Check matches on the machine readable range, which is why the resolved 3.5.11 jar is reported and why 3.5.12 is the release named here. The parent is pinned at 3.5.11 by requirement and may not be advanced unilaterally. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. No additional-path is configured for any health group: the groups are served under the standard /actuator/health/{group} paths, and the bypass requires an additional-path that collides with a secured application endpoint. Application endpoints live under /api/**, disjoint from /actuator/**. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.12 or later, then DELETE this entry. 3.5.12 clears THIS record; it does not clear the five advisories fixed in 3.5.14 that the Tier 3 aggregator entry above covers, so an upgrade intended to clear every open Spring Boot record must reach 3.5.14 or later. Configuring management.endpoint.health.group.*.additional-path requires re-examining this record first. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01.
